entry.title: SBND first results
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Short-Baseline Near Detector released its first neutrino-argon cross-section measurement, for muon-neutrino charged-current interactions with a single proton and no pions in the final state. It uses a subset of Run 1 data corresponding to 8.8×10^19 protons-on-target and selects 12,804 signal candidates with a purity of 91%. The cross sections, measured as functions of transverse kinematic imbalance variables, discriminate strongly among event-generator predictions. Fermilab presents the result as improving interaction modelling in preparation for DUNE.

entry.title: SBND exotic searches
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A separate SBND paper searches for long-lived particles produced by neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay into visible final states. It uses a subset of the Cosmic Ray Tagger that ran as a standalone detector, the CRT Beam Telescope, in 2017-2018. Full SBND neutrino data taking began in December 2024.

entry.title: CONUS+ reactor CEvNS
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CONUS+ reported what it calls the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering from reactor antineutrinos, using germanium detectors at the Leibstadt power plant. With 1296 kg·days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis gave 1555 ± 152 events at 10.2σ, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of 1701 ± 198 events within 0.6 standard deviations. The result also gives sin²θ_W = 0.225 ± 0.022 at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV. A companion paper describes the run 2 detector performance and background model, following an upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes.

entry.title: Super-Kamiokande DSNB
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Super-Kamiokande reports an indication of electron antineutrinos from the diffuse supernova neutrino background, from a spectral fit to a 5003.0-day dataset. The analysis improves the rejection of atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds, the evaluation of systematic uncertainties and the spectral fitting method. For a representative DSNB model, the best-fit flux is 3.6 (+1.6, -1.5) cm^-2 s^-1 for E_ν > 13.3 MeV, a 2.6σ tension with the null hypothesis. Similar significances were obtained with signal models of varying spectral shape.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab reports that construction of the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility is entering its next phase, with critical components arriving and partner institutions contributing. UK scientists and engineers have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies, the sensors that will detect the electrical signals from neutrino interactions in liquid argon. SLAC's machine-learning reconstruction tool SPINE is deployed in the SBN programme and DUNE.

entry.title: KM3NeT news
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The KM3NeT Collaboration has been recognised as a Landmark in the ESFRI Roadmap 2026. It held its Autumn 2026 Collaboration Meeting in Siracusa, with a five-day programme that included status updates on detector operations. A review of the event KM3-230213A, inferred parent-neutrino energy of order 10^17 eV, notes that no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been found despite extensive follow-up.

The winter-over team at the South Pole spent a week on detector maintenance and troubleshooting, including a hard-drive replacement and software updates, with calibration operations under way on the Upgrade. Another report records that the station gathered for a group photo at the IceCube Lab on learning that IceCube PI Francis Halzen had been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

entry.title: TAMBO and TAMBITO
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Tau Air-Shower Mountain-Based Observatory is designed to detect tau neutrinos from 1 PeV to 1,000 PeV. This range lies between the reach of optical-Cherenkov and radio-based experiments, and backgrounds there are largely suppressed. It will use up to 5,000 particle detectors installed on the face of a steep hill. A new proceedings paper presents the project together with the TAMBITO prototype.

entry.title: PUEO balloon mission
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The PUEO collaboration presents the design and flight of a balloon-borne antenna array. It is built to detect the Askaryan emission from ultrahigh-energy neutrino interactions. Measurements of the flux, flavour and energy of such neutrinos would constrain how ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays are accelerated and propagate.

entry.title: T2K SuperFGD
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SuperFGD, a key component of the ND280 near-detector upgrade, is a segmented plastic scintillator made of about 2 million optically isolated 1 cm³ cubes. It gives 3D images of neutrino interactions, detects protons down to a threshold of about 300 MeV/c and can measure neutron energy by time of flight. A separate paper proposes a deep neural network to distinguish electrons, photons, muons, pions and protons in it.

entry.title: The paper examines the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes, which can accompany nucleonic Urca proc
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes, which can accompany nucleonic Urca processes if Δ isobars are present in the dense cores of massive neutron stars. The authors note that the specific contribution of this channel to neutrino emission had not been explicitly evaluated. It matters for neutron-star thermal evolution, where Urca processes are dominant cooling mechanisms.

entry.title: The author builds a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the ph
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The author builds a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the photon. This produces an effective matter potential in the Sun that modifies MSW flavour conversion. The constraints use solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande, and the paper also discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: for open two-flavour oscillations, every completely positive trace-preservin
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: for open two-flavour oscillations, every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is blind to a Majorana phase. A rate anisotropy among the transverse decoherence rates can supply an environmental phase reference. This identifies when decoherence could in principle make the Majorana phase observable in oscillations.

entry.title: The authors study thermal leptogenesis in a model with a scalar quadruplet and two vectorlike fermion triplets
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study thermal leptogenesis in a model with a scalar quadruplet and two vectorlike fermion triplets. Neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model gives sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale, and the paper asks whether leptogenesis is viable there, in a way distinct from canonical seesaw leptogenesis.

entry.title: The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected as nuclear-reco
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected as nuclear-recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors). It includes varied neutron-star masses, failed supernovae that form black holes, and the nuclear equation of state. The sensitivity is larger for models with larger neutrino emission, that is, for more compact remnants.

entry.title: The authors propose a minimal extension of the Standard Model in which a single global U(1)_PQ symmetry genera
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors propose a minimal extension of the Standard Model in which a single global U(1)_PQ symmetry generates the scales of the inverse seesaw and stabilises fermionic dark matter. Light neutrino masses arise at the TeV scale, and the model predicts a strong correlation between the effective Majorana mass and the CP-violating phase. That correlation is the part a neutrino physicist can test in future experiments.
